funciones.uso_es: To open a written text or the oral presentation and set out the issue before going into detail.

expresiones.texto: Today I would like to talk about…
expresiones.nota_es: Very useful when starting the oral presentation.

expresiones.texto: The topic I am going to discuss is…
In recent years, … has become one of the most debated issues in…
Few issues have attracted as much attention as…

expresiones.nota_es: Useful for starting from an accepted idea and then qualifying it.

expresiones.texto: … is at the heart of the current debate on…
The question of whether… has long divided economists.
expresiones.nota_es: Whether introduces an alternative; do not use “if” in this register.

expresiones.texto: Let me start by putting the issue into context.

expresiones.nota_es: Better avoided in front of the examining board: it sounds colloquial.

funciones.uso_es: For the written summary and the start of the presentation: identifying the text, its source and its topic.

expresiones.nota_es: Deal with + noun or gerund: “deals with the rise of…”.
Correct but basic; better to vary it with the following ones.

expresiones.texto: This article, published in…, focuses on…

expresiones.nota_es: Address means to tackle a problem (es: “abordar”), not to direct (es: “dirigir”).

expresiones.texto: In this piece, the author sets out to show that…
The author's main contention is that…
The text raises the question of…
expresiones.nota_es: Raise a question = to put forward a question (es: “plantear una cuestión”); not “rise”.

expresiones.texto: The passage I have been given is an extract from…
expresiones.nota_es: Useful in the oral exam for presenting the text you have been given.

expresiones.texto: Drawing on…, the author argues that…
expresiones.nota_es: Drawing on = based on, using (data, studies, experience) (es: “basándose en”).

funciones.titulo_es: Summarising the ideas in the text
funciones.uso_es: To rephrase in your own words what the author says, in the third person and with a variety of reporting verbs.

expresiones.nota_es: Do not combine with “in his opinion” in the same sentence: it is redundant.

expresiones.texto: The writer goes on to explain that…
expresiones.nota_es: Go on to + infinitive = to move on to (doing something else next) (es: “pasar a”).

expresiones.texto: The author claims / maintains / contends that…
expresiones.nota_es: Claim suggests some distance: it does not guarantee that it is true.

expresiones.texto: He / She stresses the need for…
In the second part of the text, the author turns to…
expresiones.nota_es: Useful for signalling a change of topic within the text.

expresiones.texto: The author concludes by suggesting that…
expresiones.nota_es: Suggest + that + subject + verb (not “suggest to do”).

expresiones.texto: In a nutshell, the text argues that…
expresiones.nota_es: Colloquial; “In short” is better in writing.

funciones.uso_es: To structure your arguments and announce the plan of the presentation.

expresiones.nota_es: Lastly introduces the last point in a list; “at last” means “finally, after a long wait” (es: “por fin”).

expresiones.texto: I will divide my presentation into three parts.
expresiones.nota_es: Very useful for announcing your plan to the examining board.

expresiones.texto: I will first look at…, then turn to…, and finally consider…
The first point I would like to make is that…

expresiones.nota_es: A set phrase; do not overuse it.

funciones.uso_es: To add arguments or data along the same lines.

expresiones.nota_es: In formal writing, better in mid-sentence: “It also…”.
At the start of a sentence it requires inversion: “Not only does it reduce costs, but it also…”.
It is followed by a gerund: “as well as reducing costs”.
Besides = in addition (colloquial). Do not confuse with beside = next to.

expresiones.texto: Added to this is the fact that…

funciones.uso_es: To set two facts or arguments against each other.

expresiones.nota_es: It is followed by a comma and usually starts a sentence; it does not join two clauses like “but”.

expresiones.texto: On the one hand,… On the other hand,…
expresiones.nota_es: On the other hand does not introduce a mere addition: it must present a contrast.
It joins two contrasting clauses: “Exports rose, whereas imports fell”.
Unlike + noun: “Unlike Germany, Spain…”.
For the reverse relationship: “… and, the other way round,…” (es: “y, a la inversa”).
Very natural for introducing a counterweight after an argument.

funciones.uso_es: To acknowledge that the opposing argument is partly right before rebutting it.

expresiones.nota_es: It is followed by a clause with a subject and a verb; “despite” takes a noun or a gerund.

expresiones.texto: Despite / In spite of + noun or gerund
expresiones.nota_es: Never “despite of”. Example: “despite rising costs”.

expresiones.texto: While it is undeniable that…, it does not follow that…
expresiones.nota_es: A very effective structure in replies and in the oral exam.

expresiones.texto: The case for… is not without merit.
I take the point that…, but…
expresiones.nota_es: Useful in front of the examining board for answering an objection.
High register: “be that as it may” (es: “sea como fuere”).

funciones.uso_es: To explain why something happens.

expresiones.nota_es: Do not confuse them: “because of the crisis”, “because the crisis…”.
At the start of a sentence they introduce a known cause: “Since demand is weak,…”.
Best after the verb “to be”: “The fall was due to…”.

expresiones.texto: This is largely the result of…
One of the main reasons for… is…
expresiones.nota_es: Reason for + noun; reason why + clause.
Stem from = to derive from, to originate in.
Given that = since, considering that (es: “dado que”).

funciones.uso_es: To present the effects of an event or a measure.

expresiones.nota_es: In formal writing, “therefore” or “as a result” is better.
Thus also means “in this way”.
Do not confuse with “consistently” (in a constant, regular way).

expresiones.texto: This leads to… / This results in…
expresiones.nota_es: Result in = to cause; result from = to be caused by.
It can be used with a noun and no verb: “Hence the need for reform”.
In turn = as a further consequence, to link effects in a chain (es: “a su vez”).
Pave the way for = to make something possible or easier (es: “allanar el camino a”).

funciones.uso_es: To illustrate an idea with specific cases.

expresiones.nota_es: It introduces examples within the sentence: “countries such as Spain or Italy”.
In formal writing, prefer “such as”.
A clear case, a good example.
Useful in the oral exam to catch the board's attention.
Namely = that is to say; it specifies what has just been said rather than giving any example.
Only in writing and in brackets; e.g. = for example, i.e. = that is.

funciones.uso_es: To soften or limit the scope of a statement and show balanced thinking.

expresiones.texto: to some extent / to a certain extent
This is not to say that…
expresiones.nota_es: Very useful to prevent the idea from being taken to an extreme.

expresiones.texto: It depends to a large extent on…
It would be an oversimplification to say that…

expresiones.nota_es: Arguably = it could be argued that (it does not mean Spanish “discutiblemente”).
“Prices tend to rise…”: it avoids an absolute statement.
Equivalent to ceteris paribus.

funciones.uso_es: To express your position in writing or in front of the examining board.

expresiones.texto: In my opinion,… / In my view,…
expresiones.nota_es: Do not say “in my opinion, I think”: it is redundant.

expresiones.texto: As far as I am concerned,…
expresiones.nota_es: It means “as far as I am concerned”.
“From my point of view”, not “under my point of view”.
Very natural in academic register and in front of the examining board.

funciones.uso_es: To show that you share an idea from the text or from the board, fully or partly.

expresiones.texto: I agree with… / I agree that…
expresiones.nota_es: Agree is a verb: never “I am agree”.

expresiones.texto: I share the author's view that…
The author is right to point out that…

expresiones.nota_es: It expresses complete agreement, even though it contains a negative.

expresiones.texto: There is a lot of truth in…
I agree up to a point.
expresiones.nota_es: Partial agreement; it prepares the ground for a qualification.

expresiones.texto: I am inclined to agree with…
expresiones.nota_es: Cautious agreement.

funciones.uso_es: To rebut an idea politely, in a reply or in front of the examining board.

expresiones.texto: I don't agree with… / I disagree with…

expresiones.nota_es: A mild, polite way of disagreeing.

expresiones.texto: I am afraid I cannot agree with…

expresiones.nota_es: Take issue with = to disagree with, to challenge.

expresiones.texto: This argument does not stand up to scrutiny.
It is far from clear that…

expresiones.nota_es: In front of the board, only with a very polite tone: it may sound confrontational.

funciones.uso_es: To imagine scenarios, the consequences of a measure or conditions.

expresiones.nota_es: First conditional: a possible situation. If + present, will + infinitive.
Second conditional: a hypothesis. If + past, would + infinitive (“If rates rose, …”).
Third conditional: a hypothesis about the past.
Unless = except if; it takes an affirmative verb: “unless prices fall”.
As long as, on condition that (a condition).

expresiones.texto: Were the government to…, it would…
expresiones.nota_es: Conditional with inversion, high register (C1–C2).
Inversion with should = if the situation were to get worse.
In the event of + noun: “in the event of a crisis”.

funciones.uso_es: To explain an idea in a different way, especially in the oral exam if the board does not seem to have understood it.

expresiones.nota_es: Useful in the oral exam for correcting yourself without losing the thread.
Only in writing: “that is to say”.

funciones.uso_es: To close a written text or a line of reasoning and sum up the main idea.

expresiones.nota_es: Correct, but very overused: alternate it with others.
It shows that the advantages and disadvantages have been weighed up.
It means “in the end, finally” (es: “en última instancia”), not “lately, recently” (es: “últimamente”).

expresiones.texto: To conclude, I would say that…

funciones.uso_es: To think for a few seconds before answering the board without falling silent.

expresiones.nota_es: Do not overuse it: if you repeat it in every answer, it shows.

expresiones.texto: Let me think about that for a moment.
I haven't really thought about it before, but…
That's a difficult question to answer in a few words.
There are several ways of looking at this.
If I may, I would like to approach this question from two angles.
expresiones.nota_es: It lets you think and, at the same time, announce a structured answer.

expresiones.texto: I'm glad you asked that, because…

funciones.uso_es: To ask them to repeat or clarify a question without losing your composure.

expresiones.texto: Sorry, could you repeat the question, please?
I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch that.
expresiones.nota_es: Catch = to understand what you have heard.

expresiones.texto: Could you say that again, please?

expresiones.nota_es: Useful for checking that you have understood the question.

expresiones.texto: Would you mind rephrasing the question?
expresiones.nota_es: Would you mind + gerund.

expresiones.texto: If I have understood correctly, you are asking whether…
expresiones.nota_es: Recommended: it confirms the question and gives you time.

expresiones.texto: Are you referring to… or to…?
Could you clarify what you mean by…?
I'm not sure I've understood the question.

funciones.uso_es: To end the oral presentation clearly and move on to the board's questions.

expresiones.texto: To conclude, I would like to stress that…
That brings me to the end of my presentation.

expresiones.nota_es: Round off = to finish, to bring to a close.

expresiones.texto: Let me finish by saying that…
In short, the text shows that…
I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.
I hope I have given you a clear overview of…

expresiones.nota_es: Too colloquial in front of an examining board; the previous ones are better.
